Stamp Duty Land Tax - Residential property rates. You usually pay Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on increasing portions of the property price when you buy residential property, for example a house or flat. The amount you pay depends on:. • when you bought the property. • how much you paid for it. • whether you’re eligible for relief or an exemption. Rates for a single property. You pay SDLT at these rates if, after buying the property, it is the only residential property you own. You will usually pay 5% on top of these rates if you own another residential property. Rates from 1 April 2025. Property or lease premium or transfer value SDLT rate. Up to £125,000 Zero. The next £125,000 (the portion from £125,001 to £250,000) 2%. The next £675,000 (the portion from £250,001 to £925,000) 5%. The next £575,000 (the portion from £925,001 to £1.5 million) 10%. The remaining amount (the portion above £1.5 million) 12%. Example. In April 2025 you buy a house for £295,000. The SDLT you owe will be calculated as follows:. • 0% on the first £125,000 = £0. • 2% on the second £125,000 = £2,500. • 5% on the final £45,000 = £2,250. • total SDLT = £4,750. 4 BEDROOM EXTENDED DETACHED FAMILY HOME. Situated on Lodge Causeway in the popular area of Fishponds, this attractive period home offers generous and versatile accommodation arranged over two floors, combining original character features with modernised living space. The property benefits from a welcoming entrance hall, spacious reception rooms, a contemporary fitted kitchen, useful utility facilities and a delightful south-facing rear garden. The ground floor begins with an entrance hall featuring original period details, including a decorative tiled floor and stripped pitch-pine floorboards, setting the tone for the character found throughout the home. The spacious lounge provides a comfortable place to relax, featuring stripped wooden floorboards, a bay window and a cast-iron fireplace with decorative surround. This leads through to the generous dining room, which offers an excellent space for both everyday family life and entertaining. With further character features, including a cast-iron fireplace, the dining room benefits from French doors opening onto the rear decking, creating a lovely connection between the indoor living space and garden. The contemporary fitted kitchen is positioned to the rear of the property and offers a range of modern wall and floor units, oak work surfaces, an inset sink and integrated cooking facilities. Completing the ground floor is a useful rear lobby and utility area, providing additional storage, laundry facilities and access to a convenient downstairs WC. There is also access to the rear garden from this area, making it particularly practical for family life. Upstairs, the property is currently arranged as four bedrooms, with the front bedroom divided into two separate spaces. This offers flexibility for growing families, guests or those requiring a home office, nursery or dressing room. There are two further bedrooms one being a good size double and the other a single bedroom. The first-floor accommodation is served by a well-appointed family bathroom, comprising a contemporary white suite with a bath, wash basin and a separate shower cubicle. A particular highlight of the property is the delightful south-facing rear garden, which provides a wonderful outdoor retreat in an urban setting. Accessed via the rear decking and steps leading down to the garden, the outdoor space begins with a brick-laid patio before opening onto an informal lawn, bordered by established planting, mature shrubs and fruit trees. An ornamental pond and timber garden shed/studio add further interest towards the rear of the garden, while the mature greenery creates a private and inviting setting. Enjoying sunshine throughout much of the day, the garden is an ideal space for relaxing, entertaining and outdoor dining, with the sunny aspect allowing for pleasant evenings outside well into the summer. To the front of the property, an attractive garden with established shrubs, trees and bushes provides a pleasant approach. Subject to the necessary permissions and approvals, a prospective purchaser may wish to explore the possibility of creating off-street parking. The property also benefits from access to cellar storage beneath the house, providing useful additional space. Situation. Lodge Causeway enjoys a convenient position within the vibrant and well-established neighbourhood of Fishponds, offering an appealing balance of urban convenience and access to outdoor spaces. Fishponds High Street is within easy walking distance, providing a wide range of independent shops, cafés, supermarkets and everyday amenities. The area is also well placed for access to the Bristol and Bath cycle path, making it particularly appealing to cyclists and those seeking an alternative way to commute. Public transport links also provide convenient connections into Bristol and the surrounding areas. The property is well suited to families, with a choice of local primary schools and secondary education options nearby. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the surrounding area offers a number of green spaces and walking routes, including access towards the Frome Valley and Coombe Brook Nature Reserve. These provide opportunities to enjoy walking, cycling and nature while remaining close to the conveniences of an established urban neighbourhood. text: This charming 1930s home has been thoughtfully enhanced and modernised by the current owners, creating generous, extended accommodation ideally suited to modern family life. Set within a peaceful residential pocket of Brislington West, the property combines characterful features with well-planned living spaces and a lovely connection to the garden. A welcoming porch opens into the entrance hall, where a bespoke oak and glazed staircase creates an attractive first impression. The bay-fronted sitting room provides a cosy retreat, while a circular archway leads through to the dining room, where double doors open onto the garden. The kitchen has been designed with both practicality and sociability in mind, featuring shaker-style units, a breakfast bar, space for the usual appliances and views across the garden. Upstairs, the landing leads to three well-proportioned bedrooms and a four-piece family bathroom. The principal bedroom benefits from a wall of built-in wardrobes, providing useful storage without compromising on space. Outside, the gardens to the front and rear have been carefully maintained, with established planting, generous lawn areas and several seating spots offering inviting places to relax, entertain and enjoy the summer sunshine. Hulse Road enjoys a particularly appealing position, balancing a peaceful neighbourhood setting with convenient access to Bristol's amenities. Sandy Park Road is within easy reach, offering a popular selection of independent cafés, bakeries and boutiques, while nearby Victory Park and Nightingale Valley provide welcome green space for walks and outdoor recreation. Bristol City Centre is approximately 3 km away, with the A4 Bath Road and Bristol Temple Meads providing convenient connections for commuters. Combining 1930s charm, thoughtfully updated interiors and attractive gardens, this is a welcoming family home in a well-connected Bristol location, offering an appealing balance of everyday comfort and city convenience. An attractive three-bedroom end of terrace home, situated on a popular street in Brentry, close to the sought-after Primary School, and within easy reach of local shops, parks and transport links . Overview . The entrance hall opens straight into an impressive kitchen/diner, a large and sociable space with ample storage and a built-in breakfast bar, ideal for casual dining or entertaining guests. Flowing on from here, the lounge offers a comfortable, more private space to relax away from the hub of the home. At the other side a bright sun room opens out, perfect for enjoying the garden view year-round. A separate utility room and WC are accessed off the kitchen, adding to the homes practicality. Upstairs on the first floor, the landing gives access to three well-proportioned bedrooms. Both the master bedroom and second bedroom benefit from fitted wardrobes, while the third bedroom is a versatile space, equally suited to a child's room or a home office. The family bathroom fitted with a three piece suite completes the first floor. A further staircase rises to the second floor with a versatile loft room, a fantastic bonus space that could easily serve as generous storage or be transformed into a hobby room, home office, or studio. A generous timber decked terrace runs the width of the house, ideal for outdoor dining and entertaining. To one side, a substantial part-covered pergola provides a sheltered spot for a hot tub, complete with a retractable screen, perfect for year-round use. What really sets this garden apart is its open outlook: with views stretching past the boundary fence, there's a lovely feeling of space and sky that's hard to find. Location .
